data.title: Scott Aaronson says AI labs may hold unreleased math results that could weaken RSA
data.description:
For years, the big threat to RSA encryption had a familiar face: a sufficiently powerful quantum computer. Scott Aaronson is now suggesting the first crack could come from somewhere else entirely.

Aaronson is a computer science professor at the University of Texas at Austin and previously worked as a researcher at OpenAI. He says AI labs may be holding undisclosed mathematical breakthroughs that could weaken RSA before quantum machines ever show up to do the job.

On November 25, 2026, Aaronson said he is "virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources" that leading AI labs have cryptography results they have not made public. He named OpenAI and Anthropic specifically.

He said these labs could hold results or algorithms capable of undermining current cryptographic standards. The operative word is "could." Nobody outside those labs has seen the work, and Aaronson did not claim to have seen it either.

He was also careful to separate his claim from the louder version circulating online. Since mid-November 2026, rumors have spread that an AI lab has produced a polynomial-time integer factoring algorithm.

That phrase needs some unpacking. RSA's security depends on the fact that splitting a very large number into its prime factors is brutally hard for ordinary computers. A polynomial-time algorithm would make that task scale manageably as numbers grow, turning a near-impossible job into a merely tedious one.

Aaronson said he has encountered no verified evidence supporting that rumor. So his position is roughly this: labs probably have cryptography results sitting in a drawer, but the specific doomsday story going viral has not been substantiated.

The companies themselves have stayed quiet. As of November 27, 2026, neither OpenAI nor Anthropic had issued any public statement confirming a cryptography breakthrough.

Aaronson has been tracking AI's effect on mathematics for years. On October 7, 2026, he noted that AI companies were privately testing their models against cryptographic protocols.

He also pointed out a conspicuous gap. The recent wave of AI-generated math publications has delivered notable results across various fields, yet cryptographic results have been absent from those releases.

Around November 25, 2026, Google released a paper presenting a new factoring algorithm. It was regarded as theoretically interesting but not practical for breaking RSA.

He also drew a line between intellectual progress in mathematics and practical consequences for security. A clever new result about numbers does not automatically translate into an attack that works against deployed systems.

All of this lands while the security community is already preparing for a different threat. Post-quantum cryptography is the ongoing effort to build encryption that can withstand both classical computers and future quantum machines.

Aaronson's comments introduce a second variable: AI-assisted mathematics could chip away at classical assumptions on its own schedule. A threat that might emerge quietly from a private lab is much harder to plan around than quantum hardware that can be watched developing in public.

For now, the honest status is unconfirmed. A credible researcher has expressed confidence about undisclosed work, an unverified rumor is circulating that he explicitly declined to endorse, and the two labs he named have said nothing.

If AI labs are generating cryptography results and choosing not to publish them, that raises questions about disclosure. Security research has traditionally depended on findings being shared so defenders can respond.

The things to watch are fairly concrete. First, whether OpenAI or Anthropic says anything publicly about cryptography research, in either direction. Second, whether any AI-assisted cryptography results appear in published work, where outside experts can check them. Third, whether follow-up analysis of Google's factoring paper changes the assessment that it is impractical against RSA. And finally, whether Aaronson himself adds detail, since his comments are currently the main anchor for this whole conversation.

The encryption protecting much of the internet has not been shown to be broken. But one of the people best placed to judge the question thinks the labs know more than they are saying.

data.title: S&P lifts South Africa ratings on improving fiscal position
data.description:
S&P upgraded South Africa's long-term foreign currency sovereign ratings to "BB+" from "BB" on Friday, citing improving fiscal trajectory, with the government on track to post its fourth annual primary fiscal surplus in 2026.

Africa's most industrialized economy has struggled for years with weak growth, rising debt and mounting debt-service costs, but the mid-term review pointed to an improving fiscal position despite heightened global uncertainty.

"Fiscal consolidation has, and will continue, despite the conflict in the Middle East having affected real GDP growth in 2026," the global ratings agency said in a statement.

South Africa's National Treasury said earlier this month that debt-to-gross domestic product peaked at 74.6% in the 2025/26 fiscal year, below the 78.4% estimated in the 2026 mid-term budget review.

Treasury has also kept a primary budget surplus, where revenue exceeds non-interest expenditure, for three consecutive years.

S&P projects South Africa's real GDP growth of 1.3% in 2026, and an average of 1.7% over 2027-2029, supported by reforms in electricity and other sectors.

The International Monetary Fund said on Tuesday the South African economy has remained relatively resilient, owing to stronger fundamentals.

S&P assigned a "stable" outlook to the sovereign, saying continued improvements in fiscal metrics and declining government debt balance the risks posed by higher energy costs linked to the Middle East conflict.

data.title: Canada's Trans Mountain to gauge shipping interest by early January in oil pipeline expansion
data.description:
By Amanda Stephenson

The operator of Canada's Trans Mountain oil pipeline expects to launch a process by early January to gauge commercial interest in a capacity expansion by approximately 210,000 barrels per day, CEO Mark Maki said on Friday.

The process, known as an open season, would determine whether there is enough shipper interest to build Trans Mountain's Mainline Optimization Project, which would involve constructing about 30 km (19 miles) of new pipe in British Columbia and adding 11 new pump stations along the existing pipeline.

Trans Mountain is targeting April 2027 for a final investment decision on the project, Maki said in an interview, with a construction completion date in late 2028.

The Trans Mountain pipeline, owned by the Canadian government, transports oil from Alberta to BC's west coast, where it can be shipped to overseas markets including China.

Trans Mountain completed a C$34 billion ($24 billion) expansion in 2024, tripling the pipeline's capacity to 890,000 bpd. Oil sands production in Canada continues to rise, however, and the Trans Mountain system has been running full this autumn.

Late last month, Trans Mountain's operator completed a separate project that involved adding chemical additives to reduce pipeline friction, giving it the ability to increase capacity by up to 10%, or 90,000 bpd, depending on market demand.

In September, Canada's federal government sent letters to 129 First Nations along the Trans Mountain pipeline route, offering them a combined 15% equity ownership stake in the pipeline.

The government has held four confidential information sessions with First Nations about the opportunity, Maki said, adding he expects any potential equity transaction would likely take place in late 2028, after the completion of the Mainline Optimization Project.

($1 = 1.4238 Canadian dollars)

data.title: 60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals, Inc. Announces Approval of Reverse Stock Split Ratio
data.description:
WASHINGTON, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- 60 Degree Pharmaceuticals, Inc. (NASDAQ: SXTP; SXTPW) (“60 Degrees Pharma” or the “Company”), a pharmaceutical company focused on developing new medicines for vector-borne disease, today announced that it will effect a one-for-seven (1:7) reverse stock split (the "reverse split") of its common stock, par value $0.0001 per share (the "Common Stock"), that will become effective on December 2, 2026, at 12:01 AM Eastern Time, before the opening of trading on The Nasdaq Capital Market ("Nasdaq"). 60 Degrees Pharma has requested that its Common Stock begin trading on December 2, 2026, on a post-reverse split basis on the Nasdaq under the existing symbol "SXTP".

The reverse split is primarily intended to bring 60 Degrees Pharma into compliance with the minimum bid price requirement for maintaining its listing on the Nasdaq. The new CUSIP number for the Common Stock following the reverse split will be 83006G609.

At 60 Degree Pharma’s special meeting of stockholders on August 5, 2026 (the "Special Meeting"), 60 Degree Pharma’s stockholders approved the proposal to authorize 60 Degree Pharma’s board of directors (the "Board"), in its sole and absolute discretion, to file a certificate of amendment (the "Amendment") to 60 Degree Pharma’s amended and restated certificate of incorporation to effect the reverse split of the Company at a ratio of one-to-seven (1:7). On November 12, 2026, the Board approved the reverse split at a ratio of one-to-seven (1:7), and the Amendment has been filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware, which will become effective on November 30, 2026, at 12:01 AM Eastern Time, before the opening of trading on the Nasdaq.

The reverse split will affect all issued and outstanding shares of Common Stock. All outstanding options, restricted stock awards, warrants and other securities entitling their holders to purchase or otherwise receive shares of Common Stock will be adjusted as a result of the reverse split, as required by the terms of each security. The number of shares available to be awarded under any Equity Incentive Plan will also be appropriately adjusted. Following the reverse split, the par value of the Common Stock will remain unchanged at $0.0001 per share. The reverse split will not change the authorized number of shares of Common Stock or preferred stock. No fractional shares of Common Stock shall be issued as a result of the Reverse Split, and stockholders who otherwise would be entitled to receive fractional shares of New Common Stock shall be entitled to receive the number of shares of New Common Stock rounded up to the next whole number. The reverse split will affect all stockholders uniformly and will not alter any stockholder's percentage interest in 60 Degree Pharma’s equity (other than as a result of the rounding of fractional shares, as set forth above).

The reverse split will reduce the number of shares of Common Stock issued and outstanding from approximately 4,484,622 to approximately 560,578.

About 60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals, Inc.

60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals, Inc., founded in 2010, specializes in developing and commercializing new medicines for the treatment and prevention of vector-borne disease. The Company achieved U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval of its lead product, ARAKODA® (tafenoquine), for malaria prevention in 2018. ARAKODA is commercially available in the U.S. and Australia. 60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals, Inc. also collaborates with prominent research and academic organizations in the U.S. and Australia. 60 Degrees Pharmaceuticals, Inc. is headquartered in Washington, D.C., with a subsidiary in Australia. data.title: West Red Lake Gold Reports Q3 2026 Financial Results and Continued Positive Free Cash Flow
data.description:
VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- West Red Lake Gold Mines Ltd. (“West Red Lake Gold” or “WRLG” or the “Company”) OTCQX:WRLGF announces its financial and operating results for the three months ended September 30, 2026 (“Q3”) from the Madsen Mine (“Madsen”) located in the Red Lake mining district of Ontario. The Company will hold a webcast on November 30, 2026 to discuss the results. Please refer to the webcast details provided near the end of this news release for information on how to attend.

Q3 2026 Highlights

  • Gold production totaled 7,859 ounces during Q3, bringing year-to-date production to 22,102 ounces.
  • Gold sales totaled 7,737 ounces during Q3, bringing year-to-date gold sales to 22,162 ounces.
  • Revenue totaled $45.8 million and income from mine operations of $12.7 million, representing an operating margin of 28%.
  • Adjusted net earnings(2) of $5.5 million, or $0.01 per basic share, bringing year-to-date adjusted net earnings of $24.5 million, or $0.06 per basic share.
  • Adjusted EBITDA(2) of $15.6 million, bringing year-to-date adjusted EBITDA to $52.1 million.
  • Cash costs(1)(2) of US$2,400 per ounce sold and All-in sustaining costs (“AISC”)(1)(2) of US$3,985(1) per ounce sold, reflecting lower gold production and sales during the quarter.
  • Generated $1.9 million in positive free cash flow, marking the second consecutive quarter of positive free cash flow.
  • The Company ended the quarter with approximately $18.8 million in cash and cash equivalents.

Shane Williams, President and CEO, commented, “Madsen continued to generate positive free cash flow in the third quarter, bringing year-to-date revenue to $136.6 million, adjusted EBITDA to $52.1 million and free cash flow to $5.4 million in our first nine months of commercial production. Although underground mining challenges impacted production and unit costs during the quarter, we continued to advance key operational and infrastructure initiatives to support improved operating performance.”

“Our immediate focus remains on improving underground mining productivity and advancing development to establish additional mining fronts. During the quarter, we supplemented our underground workforce with specialized contractors, commissioned the secondary crusher and continued to invest in underground development and infrastructure.”

“As we advance access to new mining areas, including the 904 Complex and the Fork deposit, we expect to benefit from greater operating flexibility and a more consistent production profile as we move into 2027. Our recently announced Integrated Pre-Feasibility Study builds on these investments and defines a clear pathway to growing production and extending mine life, with Madsen serving as the central hub of our district-scale strategy in Red Lake.”

Financial Results

Financial performance during Q3 reflected lower gold production and sales relative to the three months ended June 30, 2026 (“Q2”), together with higher unit operating costs and sustaining capital expenditures. Despite these challenges, the Company maintained positive operating margins and generated positive free cash flow for the second consecutive quarter.

Gold sales totaled 7,737 ounces during Q3 at an average realized gold price of US$4,230 per ounce, generating revenue of $45.8 million, compared with $49.0 million in Q2. Income from mining operations totaled $12.7 million, with an operating margin of 28%, compared with $20.1 million and 41%, respectively, in Q2.

Adjusted EBITDA totaled $15.6 million, compared with $22.1 million in Q2, while adjusted net earnings totaled $5.5 million, or $0.01 per basic share, compared with $12.6 million, or $0.03 per basic share, in Q2.

Cash costs increased to US$2,400 per ounce sold, compared with US$2,000 per ounce in Q2. AISC increased to US$3,985 per ounce sold, compared with US$3,284 per ounce in Q2, lower gold sales and an increase in sustaining capital expenditures to $14.5 million from $12.3 million in Q2.

The Company generated $1.9 million of positive free cash flow during Q3, bringing year-to-date free cash flow to $5.4 million. The Company ended the quarter with approximately $18.8 million in cash and cash equivalents.

During the first nine months of commercial production at Madsen, the Company generated $136.6 million in revenue, $48.1 million in income from mining operations and $52.1 million in adjusted EBITDA.

Operating Results

As reported in the Company's operational update dated October 27, 2026 (see news release dated October 27, 2026), gold production totaled 7,859 ounces during Q3, bringing year-to-date production to 22,102 ounces.

During Q3, the Company mined 63,945 tonnes at an average grade of 3.8 g/t Au, compared with 74,604 tonnes at 4.1 g/t Au in Q2. Underground mining performance was impacted by the complexities associated with remnant pillar extraction and the availability of skilled underground personnel. Specialized contractors were brought in to support mining activities and maintain development progress.

Mill performance continued to improve, with average throughput increasing to 867 tonnes per day (“tpd”) from 842 tpd in Q2, while gold recovery averaged 94%. The commissioning of the secondary crusher during Q3 addressed material-handling constraints and supported increased processing capacity. Lower-grade ore stockpiled during Q2 was also processed during the quarter.

Underground development progressed during Q3, with a focus on expanding production inventory and establishing additional mining fronts. Continued development toward non-remanent areas.

2026 Outlook

The Company remains on track to achieve its revised 2026 gold production guidance of 27,000 to 32,000 ounces.

For the balance of 2026, the Company will continue to invest in underground development and infrastructure, together with the transition into new mining areas, including the 904 Complex and the Fork deposit, expected to provide greater operating flexibility and support a more consistent production profile in 2027.

About West Red Lake Gold Mines

West Red Lake Gold Mines Ltd. is a Canadian gold producer and developer advancing a high-grade, district scale opportunity in the Red Lake district of Ontario. The Company’s flagship Madsen Mine has recently achieved commercial production and is positioned as the central hub of a growing multi asset platform. The Company controls a 47 km² land package in one of the world’s most prolific mining districts, which has historically produced over 20 million ounces of gold from high grade systems1. data.title: Hayasa Metals Reports Final 2026 Urasar Drill Results and Outlines its Strategic Focus
data.description:
A Major Mining Company Sole Funding a Minimum Two-Year Exploration Alliance Under September Term Sheet

Three New Licenses Expected in Early 2027, Vardenis Option Ended to Remove Carrying Costs

Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 27, 2026) - Hayasa Metals Inc. (OTCQB: HAYAF) ("Hayasa" or the "Company") reports geochemical and assay results from two diamond drill holes totaling 1,052.9 meters ("m") from the western zone of the Company's Urasar Project in northern Armenia.

2026 Drilling Highlights

  • Both holes intersected strong to intense hydrothermal alteration and stockwork veining, consistent with the upper levels of a porphyry-style system.

  • Copper and gold grades were low; mineralized core of the system has not yet been intersected.

  • Hayasa controls 100% of Urasar; seeks a partner for the next phase.

Diamond drill hole UDD-022 tested the Oxide Basin prospect and returned 21.0 m grading 0.08% copper ("Cu") and 0.12 g/t gold ("Au") from 321 to 342 m depth, including 4.0 m with 0.33% Cu and 0.35 g/t Au.

The 21 m elevated gold interval occurs within a longer anomalous interval of 124 m averaging 0.04% Cu and 0.035 g/t Au from 256 to 380 m. The highest individual copper and gold sample in this program returned 0.5% Cu and 0.4 g/t Au from 338 to 340 m.

Hole UDD-023 tested the Silica West zone and returned narrower intervals of elevated copper, including 1.2 m grading 0.2% Cu from 330.8 to 332.0 m. A separate 8.0 m interval from 366 to 374 m averaged 0.05% Cu, and a single 1.6 m sample from 116.3 m returned 19.6 g/t silver ("Ag"). Both holes intersected strong to intense hydrothermal alteration and stockwork veining.

Table 1. Selected 2026 assay results

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

Intervals are downhole lengths. True widths are unknown. Composite grades are weighted by sample length using all samples within each stated interval. The 124.0 m interval describes a broad sampled section, with no grade cutoff applied.

2026 Drilling and Geological Interpretation

This recent drill program tested steeply oriented low-resistivity targets identified on two Audio Magneto Telluric (AMT) profiles at the western end of the Urasar license. Final collar records confirm a combined depth of 1,052.9 m, which is revised from the 1,070 m reported on September 4, 2026. The drill hole targeting was based on the May 2026 six-line, 53-station AMT survey, surface geochemistry and mapped alteration, as well as an earlier 39 m drill intercept averaging 0.50% Cu and 0.18 ppm Au intersected in Hole UDD-021 in Oxide Basin. The two-hole 2026 drill program returned lower copper values than UDD-021 over the broader intervals reported here. These weakly mineralized intervals are hosted in similar brecciated and altered lithologies as intersected in UDD-021.

Both holes intersected multiphase quartz-anhydrite veining with ubiquitous pyrite accessory chalcopyrite, and occasional enargite in strong to intense argillic to advanced argillic alteration. Potassic alteration was observed at depth. These characteristics are consistent with the upper levels of a porphyry-style hydrothermal system.

Figure 1. 2026 drillholes Oblique 3D view showing UDD-022 (Oxide Basin) and UDD-023 (Silica West) in black, 2024-2025 drillholes in blue.

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/3169/326239_8ef5234b6428499e_003full.jpg

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

https://images.newsfilecorp.com/files/3169/326239_8ef5234b6428499e_003full.jpg

Oxide Basin UDD-022

UDD-022 was completed to 622.0 m and encountered intense silicification from 170.1 to 254.6 m, followed by predominantly propylitic alteration with local silicification and repeated stockwork intervals. The strongest copper and gold values fall within a fault zone from 335.4 to 343.5 m, in a porphyritic unit. Farther downhole, stockwork veining was intersected from 390.0 to 457.6 m and from 483.0 to 503.0 m.

Silica West UDD-023

UDD-023 was completed to 430.9 m. The hole intersected shallow argillic and sericitic alteration, silicification from 44.2 to 224.9 m, and predominantly propylitic alteration from 224.9 m to the end of the hole. Stockwork veining was encountered from 141.0 to 236.1 m and from 264.8 to 430.9 m (end of hole). The higher copper assays occur as short intervals within this lower altered sequence.

Table 2. As-drilled collar data

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

Azimuths and dips are collar orientations. Coordinates are shown in the project grid as recorded in the collar file. RL is collar elevation

Figure 2. Selected core pictures illustrating local textures in the two holes.

To view an enhanced version of this graphic, please visit:

Management Comments

Hovo Karapetyan, Chief Geologist and Country Manager, commented: "The pervasive strong to intense alteration, extensive brecciation and widespread sulfide mineralization encountered to date indicate that we are operating within a large and strongly developed hydrothermal system. While our exploration program has completed 23 holes totaling over 5,000 meters, we have yet to intersect the mineralized core of the system. However, the widespread presence of anomalous, albeit low-grade, gold, base metal and arsenic values indicate that we are exploring in the right geological environment. Further analysis of the extensive Hayasa exploration database, together with historical Soviet-era data, is underway to refine our geological understanding and better vector future exploration towards the mineralized core of the system."

Hayasa CEO, Joel Sutherland, adds: "We have now drilled more than 5,000 m at Urasar. These two holes returned lower grades than we were looking for, but the drill core still indicates a system whose center we have yet to find. There is a decent amount of inbound interest on Urasar, the property is 34 km2 and there are additional zones to explore. We will announce our plans on Urasar in early 2027."

Sampling and Analytical Quality Control

Hayasa's local geological team split and sampled the drill core in Armenia. Samples were prepared at the accredited Institute of Mining and Metallurgy in Armenia and analyzed by ALS in Romania, where the laboratory operates to international standards. The 2026 assay workbook lists 590 downhole sample intervals and records ALS methods Au-AA23 (30 g fire assay with an atomic absorption finish for gold) and ME-ICP61 (four-acid digestion with an ICP-AES finish for multi-element analysis).

Hayasa inserted one QA/QC control sample every 20 m of drilling. The control samples comprised standards, duplicates and blanks.

Portfolio Focus and Termination of Vardenis Option

The Company has elected to terminate its option with Mendia Resources on the Vardenis property in central Armenia after the withdrawal of our former partner. This removes the carrying costs of the property and lets the Company concentrate on its strategic exploration alliance with a major mining company in southern Armenia and on the three new exploration licenses it expects to receive in early 2027.

As announced on September 21, 2026, Hayasa signed a term sheet with a major mining company for a strategic exploration alliance focused on copper and other critical metals in southern Armenia. Under the term sheet, the alliance phase has a term of two years and is solely funded by the major mining company. After US$1,000,000 has been spent within the alliance area of interest, the major mining company may earn a 51% interest in a designated project by funding US$1,000,000 on that project over two years, and may increase its interest to 70% by funding a further US$3,000,000 over three years. Hayasa is the operator during the first option period. The term sheet is non-binding except for certain limited provisions, and the alliance remains subject to the negotiation and execution of definitive agreements, which are expected before year end.

As previously announced (see news releases dated April 2 and May 11, 2026), the three license applications are Amasia in northern Armenia, an antimony-nickel-cobalt prospect, Hovo's Reward and Mount Stephanie in central Armenia, which host copper-silver and copper-gold surface anomalies, respectively.

Mr. Sutherland, adds: "Vardenis did a lot for Hayasa Metals and we arguably would not be in a strategic alliance without the work we performed there. We completed robust geophysics and drilled over 5,000 m and worked with an exceptional team of drillers and geologists. We have a lot going on in 2027 with the strategic alliance activity accelerating and the addition of three new exploration licenses."

Qualified Person

The content of this news release was reviewed and approved by Dennis Moore, Hayasa's President and Chairman, a qualified person as defined by National Instrument 43-101.

On behalf of the Board of Directors,

Joel Sutherland

CEO

data.title: Adani seeks government nod to invest in airlines, eyes bigger role in India's aviation market
data.description:
Adani Group has approached the government seeking permission to invest in the airline sector, signalling a possible expansion of its aviation interests beyond airport operations as it sees scope for a significant increase in India's air traffic capacity.

Group chief financial officer Jugeshinder Robbie Singh said on Friday that India needs nearly 10 times its current daily flight capacity, to around 30,000 flights, to cater to the potential passenger base.

"And that's why we requested the government to at least allow us to invest, so that we can facilitate the development of airlines. Some fund, some other airline company and things like that...or an entrepreneur who wants to go into that space," Singh told reporters on the sidelines of the India Debt Capital Market Summit.

Adani sees room for more airlines

Singh said more than 60 crore people in India have the potential to fly, pointing to the need for greater airline capacity to accommodate the country's untapped aviation demand.

The group's request comes amid calls for greater competition in India's airline industry, which has effectively become a duopoly dominated by Tata Group-owned Air India and Rahul Bhatia-led IndiGo. The two carriers together control around 90% of the domestic aviation market.

Operational disruptions at IndiGo last year, which triggered thousands of flight cancellations, also fuelled demands for more airlines and greater competition in the sector.

Earlier denials of airline ambitions

The latest comments come despite the group's earlier indications that it was not looking to enter the airline business directly.

In July this year, the Adani Group had said it was "not evaluating any proposal to enter the airlines business". On November 3, Adani Airport Holdings chief executive Arun Bansal had also ruled out an airline venture, arguing that competing with customers was never a good strategy.

The group operates eight airports across India, including Mumbai, Navi Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow and Guwahati. Its airport network handles more than a fourth of the country's air passenger traffic, giving it a substantial presence in India's aviation infrastructure.

Singh's remarks, however, suggest the group is seeking a broader role in the airline ecosystem, potentially by enabling investments in existing carriers, funds or entrepreneurs looking to enter the sector.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: Volkswagen being singled out, rivals also paying 10% tax for parts imports, says German automaker
data.description:
MUMBAI: German automaker Volkswagen (VW) told a Mumbai court that rival companies, including BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Kia are also importing car parts into India at a 10% customs duty, arguing it has been unfairly singled out in a $1.2 billion tax dispute, Reuters reported on Friday.

In a court filing dated November 10, VW's India unit, Skoda Auto Volkswagen India, said the government's contention that other carmakers paid 30% duty while it alone paid 10% was "factually incorrect". The tax demand against the company "deserves to be quashed" if other automakers are allowed to follow the same import model, it argued. To support its case, VW submitted a table citing 2024 import data for BMW, Mercedes-Benz, Kia, Isuzu Motors and JSW MG Motor. BMW had 390,360 major shipments of car components during the year, while Mercedes-Benz had 80,972, all imported under the lower tariff category, Reuters reported citing a court filing.

VW maintained its rivals import components for assembling vehicles in India, much like it does, and that it is being selectively targeted. However, it would need to establish that its competitors' imports were similarly used to assemble complete vehicles to strengthen its argument, Reuters reported, citing people familiar with the matter.

VW is challenging a record tax demand over allegations that it deliberately imported components in separate consignments at 10% duty and assembled them into complete cars in India, thereby avoiding the higher tariffs of around 30% applicable to car kits.

Indian tax authorities have described the company's conduct as one of "fraud and subterfuge". VW has denied any wrongdoing, warning that the demand could wipe out its investments in India, where it has about 2% market share.

The Mumbai court is scheduled to hear matter on Monday. It is likely to rule initially only on whether tax authorities were entitled to scrutinise company's imports going back 12 years. The dispute highlights continuing concerns among foreign investors over India's tariff regime, with prolonged investigations and litigation creating uncertainty for businesses.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: S&P cuts Tata Motors PV ratings on weaker JLR margins, poor cash
data.description:
Mumbai: S&P Global Ratings on Friday downgraded the credit ratings of Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles (TMPV) and its wholly-owned units, stating weaker-than-expected operating performance at Jaguar Land Rover (JLR) is weighing on total profits and cash flows. The rating agency lowered its long-term issuer credit rating on TMPV and unit TML Holdings to 'BBB-' from 'BBB', while revising the outlook to stable from negative. It cut JLR's rating to 'BB+' from 'BBB-', also with a stable outlook against a negative outlook earlier.

"Weak profitability and negative free operating cash flow (FOCF) at Jaguar Land Rover Automotive PLC will likely delay financial recovery at Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles," S&P said.

British luxury carmaker JLR, which contributes about 80% of TMPV's consolidated revenue, is expected to remain a drag on the Indian automaker's earnings. S&P estimates TMPV's adjusted Ebitda margin will improve marginally to about 0.4% in FY27 from 0.2% last year.

The agency expects JLR to face continued pressure from weak sales volume and challenging market conditions. Sales of imported vehicles in China fell 35% year-on-year in the first half of FY27, further clouding the automaker's recovery prospects. S&P has pushed back its expectation of JLR turning free cash flow positive to FY28 from FY27, citing the weaker operating environment.

JLR's financial performance has also been hit by restructuring-related costs and a major product portfolio refresh.

The company reported exceptional items of 530 million in the September quarter, including separation costs and write-downs of intangible assets under development. It has lowered its full-year revenue guidance to 25 billion and expects a pre-tax margin of 2-3%, citing geopolitical risks and restructuring costs.

S&P expects JLR's annual capital expenditure and research and development spending to remain elevated at 3.3-3.4 billion over FY27 and FY28 as it undertakes the portfolio refresh. This is expected to result in adjusted negative FOCF of about 1.4 billion in FY27.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com

data.title: Centre floats urea import tender ahead of next sowing season
data.description:
New Delhi: India's National Fertilizers has invited bids for the import of urea, as the government seeks to ensure timely availability of the key fertiliser for the upcoming sowing season.

The tender, issued on behalf of the Department of Fertilizers under the Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers on November 27, seeks offers with preference for the earliest arrivals into India. According to the notice inviting tender, shipments from loading ports must be completed by January 31, 2027.

The deadline for submission of bids is December 8, 2026. The import tender comes amid the government's efforts to maintain adequate fertiliser supplies for farmers. Urea is the most widely consumed fertiliser in India and is heavily subsidised by the centre.<meta content="cms.article3" name="cmsei-article3"/> For Reprint Rights: timescontent.com
